input.brief: concept preview for Saxena Music Classes, a music school at Talwandi, Kota

direction.name: The clear service
direction.idea: People come to a service page with questions: what is it, is it for me, what does it cost, how do I start. Answer them in that order, plainly, and the page feels trustworthy. The idea is the one thing this service does that others do not, stated in the first line and proven in the rest.
direction.composition: The first screen states what the service is and for whom, with the action (book, apply, call) and one picture of the real place or people at work. Then: who it is for, as a short list; how it works, as three or four plain steps; the prices or terms, as a table; answers to real questions, as an accordion that opens one at a time; how to reach them, with the address, hours and a map or directions. The action stays reachable on every screen.
direction.typography: A friendly, readable sans or a warm serif for headings; text at a comfortable size.
direction.colour: A light ground, ink, one warm or calm accent for the action.
direction.imagery: Real pictures of the place and the people at work (the project's own, generated, or honestly generic); never stock handshakes.
direction.richness: Complete, honest answers: the real prices, the real hours, the real steps.
direction.pitfalls: Vague claims instead of facts; testimonials nobody gave; icons for every step; the booking hidden at the bottom.

hero.name: The answer first
hero.blueprint: The headline says what the service is and for whom; one sentence; the action. Beside or under it one real picture of the place or the people at work. Beside it, the headline is 5vw or more (72px at 1440); a headline that cannot be that large goes above the picture, or over it full-bleed. Under both, three or four facts a visitor would otherwise search for (price from, where, when, how long a stay or a session lasts, never a travel time the brief does not give), each a short line at the lead step that says the whole fact ("From 39 € a night, breakfast included"), never a band of big figures over one-word labels. The facts are true and complete.
hero.mobile: Headline, sentence, action, picture, then the facts as a short list.
hero.headline: What it is and for whom, three to eight words; at most about 28 characters when it stands beside the picture.

palette.name: Near-black (warm), rich magenta
palette.note: Near-black ground (#181410), light ink, one rich magenta accent. The accent is for the primary action, links and at most one other thing on a screen; it is never a ground for text blocks, never a second headline colour and never spread across cards. Two grounds, no field: the page ground and --surface, a clear step from it; sections are told apart by space, size and pictures. Every other colour on the page comes from photographs or the product, never from added tints, badges or chips.

type.name: Prata over Chillax

text.settings: weight 400 for running text, 600 for emphasis and buttons, leading 1.5, 60-72 characters a line

type.note: A serif display over a sans. A 1.333 scale from a 17px body; the hero's display step is about 5.8vw at 1440. Six steps and no others: small, body, lead, sub, head, display. Prata only for the display and head steps; Chillax for everything a visitor reads at length, buttons and navigation included. Load only the weights listed; a weight the face lacks is faked by the browser and the inspector fails it.

motion.name: Pushed line
motion.description: One line of very large type, the name or the claim, is pushed sideways by the scroll rather than by a clock: it travels from 12% right to 12% left of its place while it crosses the screen, linear and locked to the scrollbar, and reads whole at the middle of its run. One per page, never across running text, and the words must never be cropped at the moment the line sits in the middle of the screen. Build with animation-timeline: view() on the line and a translateX keyframe; static where scroll timelines are unsupported and under reduced motion.

sections.name: Lead line over four columns
sections.blueprint: Two parts on one 12-column grid with 20px margins. First, a lead paragraph of 30–40 words spans all 12 columns at clamp(22px, 2.2vw, 32px), regular weight, leading 1.2: three lines that read as the opening of a text, with no heading before it. 72px below, four equal columns (three grid columns each, 24px gutters) carry small text at 14–15px with leading 1.45. Each column is one paragraph of 40–70 words that opens with a bold run-in phrase of two or three words in full ink, the rest continuing on the same line in the soft ink. Columns top-align and end ragged at different depths. No cards, icons or dividers; the bold run-ins are the only markers. The four columns answer four plain questions: who, what, where, how to reach them. Padding is modest, 96px top and bottom, so the next section can start straight after.
sections.mobile: The lead paragraph at 20px, full width. The four columns become a two-by-two grid with a 20px gutter and 40px row gap at 14px; if any paragraph exceeds 60 words, switch to one column with 32px between paragraphs. Run-in phrases stay bold.

sections.name: One-size name columns
sections.blueprint: Pure text at one size. Three columns start on columns 1, 4 and 7 of the 12-column grid, leaving columns 10–12 empty on purpose. Each column opens with a group name in full ink and continues with a tight stack of six to ten capability names in the soft ink, all at 16–17px, regular weight, line-height 1.25, no bullets and no symbols; one blank line separates group name from stack. Hovering a name brings it to full ink and shows a one-line description in a fixed spot: the top of the empty columns 10–12, at the same size. The heading is no larger than 28px; two or three words, alone on column 1, 96px above the columns. Give the section 20vh of empty ground above and below, so the smallness reads as decided. Works on light or deep grounds.
sections.mobile: Columns stack with 40px between groups; text rises to 18px with line-height 1.4 for touch. Group names stay in full ink. Hover descriptions are dropped; each group ends instead with one sentence in the soft ink that sums it up. The heading is 24px, 48px above.

sections.name: One image across tiles
sections.blueprint: One photograph is cut across a board of tiles. A grid of six columns and four rows with 8px gaps spans the full width between 12px margins; every tile is square (aspect-ratio: 1). Each tile shows its own piece of the same image: set the photograph as every tile's background at background-size: 600% 400% and step background-position by column and row, so the picture reads whole through the gaps. Five of the twenty-four tiles are swapped for flat colour tiles from the palette, never two adjacent: one holds the heading (two to four words at 2.6vw, top-left, 16px padding), three hold one fact each at 18px, one holds the action. On hover a tile's piece scales to 108% inside its own clip. Choose a photograph with one clear subject, so the board is legible at a glance.
sections.mobile: Three columns by six rows with 6px gaps, the photograph re-cut at background-size 300% 600% from a portrait crop. Four colour tiles only; the heading tile spans two columns in the top row with the heading at 6vw. Facts drop to 15px.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

references.name: The state of the gallery
references.idea: A year-in-review told as a flight over a glowing particle landscape, where each statistic or pick is a single word floating in 3D space.
references.hero: The desktop capture caught the loader: a blue-black screen with a faint dot grid, a 4px acid-yellow progress bar across the top edge, the small logo centred at the top, and a percentage counter at 13.9vw (200px) in thin pale blue-grey grotesk anchored bottom-left. The loaded hero, seen on mobile, splits the title in two: the first two words top-left and the last three bottom-right at the same giant size, with a centred uppercase paragraph between them, all over a full-bleed terrain of olive-green haze and yellow particles. Tiny capital labels occupy all four corners.
references.type: Overused Grotesk only, regular weight: display words at 5 to 14vw in pale blue-grey with a faint lilac sheen, small parenthesised counts set as superscripts beside them, and 10px uppercase captions and corner labels. Two sizes and no bold.
references.colour: #08090d #515721 #b9c6cd #e6f21a #c8b9ee — Blue-black ground; the olive-to-acid-yellow glow of the particle field is the single colour. Type is cool pale grey with a lilac tint, and the yellow loader bar is the brightest element.
references.imagery: A procedural landscape of soft olive fog ridges with thousands of yellow-white points streaming toward the horizon in perspective; later, a curved floor of small tilted white tiles standing for catalogued sites. No photographs.
references.layout: One pinned canvas with a text overlay. Four corner labels stay fixed; each scroll step puts a single word or name at the centre with a one-line caption beneath it in the lower third. Nothing else appears on screen.

sections.description: Full-bleed particle terrain. One category word is centred at about 5vw in pale iridescent grotesk, with its count in parentheses set small and raised at the word's top-right like a superscript. A single-line uppercase caption at 10px sits centred roughly 20% below. Behind the word the particles briefly cluster into the shape of a large numeral. Corner labels are unchanged.

A top-pick slide: a tiny uppercase label above, then the pick's name centred at about 5vw and partly occluded by the scene. Below it dozens of small white rectangular tiles lie on a curved, receding floor grid, some flat and some tilting up toward the camera, growing larger toward the bottom edge of the viewport. A one-line caption sits under the name.

steal: Split a title in two and pin the halves to opposite corners, top-left and bottom-right, at the same giant size with the supporting paragraph centred between them.
Attach a count to a big word as a small parenthesised superscript at its top-right instead of building a stat card.
Make the loading percentage the first giant typographic element, anchored bottom-left under a full-width accent progress bar.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas is the only surface: a particle landscape covers 99% of the first screen with the title straight on it, and as you travel the particles leave the ground to form numerals, a figure, floating screenshot cards and a tile-grid panel, while streams of thumbnail tiles fly low between beats. No img or video elements.
references.motion: A percentage preloader is still at 89% at 4.5s, though the load event fired at 2.1s; after it the wheel is captured, each step easing the camera forward to the next beat, with text-free fly-through steps between them (5 of 13 screens show only terrain). Characters rise with a stagger, transform and opacity over 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) on 704 spans, 0.42s for secondary lines, and counts pop in with an overshoot from 0.6 to 1.08 to 1.

scenes.name: Type sets like wet ink
scenes.principle: Display type exists first as swollen, merged ink blobs and sharpens into clean letters line by line as it reaches its place on screen, because a blur is pushed through a hard alpha threshold that relaxes as the blur clears, so words seem to set like wet ink rather than fade in.
scenes.freshTake: For a mineral-water brand's manifesto, set four short lines of a heavy round grotesk in one ink on a flat chalk ground, one line per screen of native scroll. Each line condenses out of chunky blobs as it rises from the lower third to the centre, and stays crisp once set, with the blur at 8px at most, so the reader sets the pace line by line; the last line stays crisp with the one button under it. Nothing else on the page melts: every other heading cuts or slides plainly, no accent colour in the lines, no paragraph or drawings around them.
scenes.breaksWhen: Thin, light or serif faces lose their hairlines in the threshold and settle looking bolder than set. Over photographs or busy grounds the blobs read as dirt. One SVG filter per line is costly: more than four or five moving at once stutters on phones and in some browsers, so attach the filter only while a line moves and remove it at rest. Fonts must load before the lines are split. Reduced motion needs a plain cut to crisp type. Used on every heading of a page it becomes a tic.

scenes.name: Thumbnail becomes the stage
scenes.summary: A statement of one or two lines at display size sits over a row of large thumbnails on the layout's columns, whose middle one is a keyhole onto a full-screen chapter; from the first step of the scroll the keyhole grows over its neighbours as they slide in under it, rises and opens to full bleed, and the statement passes through its edge, ink outside and paper inside, sliding from centred to flush left to become the chapter's heading word for word. It opens a product, a place or a film chapter from one strong muted loop or one strong picture.
scenes.place: In the middle, as the door from the intro into the showcase or the work; the opened picture carries the chapter's feature notes on a solid band at its foot, and below 600px they follow it in the page's flow.
scenes.content: One chapter picture or muted loop of 8-15 s (16:9, 1920x1080 or more, 8MB at most, with a poster; for software, a screen recording of the product), its subject in the centre: the keyhole opens on about the central half of its width and three quarters of its height on desktop (that crop is the thumbnail); its upper left calm and dark for the white heading; a 4:5 cut for phones. One or two satellite stills a side of neighbouring chapters in the same grade, 960px wide or more with the subject in the centre (the row crops them close to square on desktop, 3:4 on tablets, 3:5 on phones). No text burned into the pictures. A statement of up to two lines of 20 characters or fewer that names the chapter and becomes its heading word for word; an optional note under the heading; three or four feature items of a 2-3 word label and 16 words or fewer.
scenes.options: hold 2 (1.4-2.6); phoneHold 1.6 (1.4-2.6); phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub 0.5, true with Lenis (0-0.8); thumb, the layout's columns by default (0.12-0.5; a share under the columns is lifted to them, a larger one runs the neighbours off the edges); radius, the page's --radius or 0 (0-16 px), always 0 at full bleed; shade 0.3 (0-0.6) flat scrim over the picture under the heading; band 1 (0-1) the band under the notes, solid by default; heading 0.15 (0.1-0.25) where the heading settles, the statement starting at the same height; nav '', the selector of a fixed nav that gets is-on-dark over the picture.
scenes.phone: The same opening with the keyhole starting at 64% of the width, 3:5, its neighbours running off the edges; hold 1.6. From 600px all four notes show two by two on the band; below 600px wide or under 540px tall they leave the stage and follow the picture in the page's flow, every one shown.

nav.text: A band that names where you are: fixed at the top, 56px tall, a solid band of the page ground on every screen. The wordmark at the left margin at the h4 step; at the right margin a Menu text button beside the one action (40px tall); dead centre the name of the section in view at 16px in the ink: the section's one- or two-word name (its link in Menu), never a sentence or a number. When the next section takes the screen the old name slides up out of a 24px mask and the new one slides up in (280ms, ease-out); over the hero the centre is empty. Menu opens the section names full-screen on the ink, with the action and the email. On a phone: a 56px band with the wordmark, Menu and the action; the live name is dropped.
nav.signature: The centre of the fixed 56px band shows the name of the section in view and swaps it by sliding the old name up out of a mask.

footer.text: A split footer: a photograph of the subject on the left six columns, from the left margin, 60svh tall; on the right six columns, on the surface tone, the closing line at the h3 step, the button, the contact, the links and the legal line, 32px between the groups.
footer.signature: A 60svh photograph on the left six columns beside the closing line, the button, the contact and the links on the surface tone.

cards.text: One large panel a section: a single filled card in the surface tone, 8-10 columns wide, 48-64px padding, holding one group whole (the price and everything it includes, the visit block, the booking choices), beside or under the section heading on the ground. Nothing framed inside it.
cards.signature: One large filled panel 8-10 columns wide holding one whole group, beside or under its heading.

buttons.text: An ink pill with an arrow chip at its end: 48px tall at 1440, fully round, the label 16px at the type system's button weight in sentence case in the ground colour with 24px left padding, and a 32px round chip inset 8px from the right end holding a 14px arrow (the chip in the ground colour with an ink arrow). Hover (250ms) rolls the label (a copy rising from below) and turns the chip to the accent with the accent's ink arrow. Reduced motion swaps the chip colour only. Use it as the action that closes a statement; 32px of space under the sentence above. Second action: the label alone in the ink with the arrow, no pill. Colour roles: ground = page, ink = pill, ground colour = chip, accent = chip on hover. Phone: Pill 48px tall with the chip kept inset, full width in a stacked block; the roll runs once on tap. House rules for it: Opaque, filled, no stroke or shadow.
buttons.signature: A 48px ink pill with a 32px round chip inset 8px at its right end; on hover the label rolls up and the chip turns the accent.
buttons.name: Opaque pill with arrow chip

corners.text: Square corners on pictures, cards, panels and fields.

spacing.text: Airy: 22-28vh between sections (200-250px at 1440, 112-140px on a phone), page margins 48-72px at 1440 and 24px on a phone.

treatment.text: One grade over every picture (slightly warm or slightly cool, a little lifted shadows), the same on all of them.

interaction.text: No interactive widget. The page is read: its content, pictures and motion carry it. Controls are the navigation, the links, the action and any real form.

clip.text: No video. Motion comes from the page itself.

entrance.name: Set type
entrance.summary: headline lines rise from masks; the picture opens like a blind
entrance.sees: The headline's lines rise out of their own baselines one after another while the picture opens downward like a blind; the sentence and the action rise 12 px after them.
entrance.markup: Wrap each headline line: `…`, three at most, with breaks that fit on one line at every width down to 360 px (a smaller display step on phones if they must).

byImagery.interface: The frame opens over the fragment, and the fragment settles from 1.08.
byImagery.type-only: Lines, then sentence and action; there is no picture step.

below.label: Headings by line
below.rule: Chapter headings (data-lines, five at most) rise line by line from their masks once, using the "Lines that rise on scroll" script in motion.md. Nothing else enters, and a stray data-reveal does nothing.

moves.name: Alternate side slide
moves.description: Three or four rows, each full width inside the page margins (about 1296px at 1440): one big photograph tile (560x560, the dealt corner) and a caption block (a title at the head step and one paragraph of about 20 words at 20px, 44 characters wide) filling the other half, so no row is empty at the left. Odd rows put the tile on the left, even rows on the right. As a row crosses from 90% to 50% of the viewport height the tile slides 180px into its place from its outer side and the caption 180px into its place from the opposite side, scrubbed, both fully visible throughout; at rest both are in place. Every row sits on the same ground, with no second fill. The dealt section space between rows. Phone: tile above caption, each moves 40px from alternating sides. House rules for it: The tile is a photograph, never a digit or a headline in a card (no 01/02/03 numbering); no outlined tiles; no row left empty on one side; scroll-linked, nothing starts hidden.

moves.name: Mask roll swap
moves.description: When a state changes (a slide, a tab, a disc, a list item) the text that describes it, a title, a price, a date or a one-to-three-word value at the lead, sub or head step, rolls out and the new text rolls in. The old text moves up 100 percent out of a mask that is exactly one line tall plus 0.1em at the bottom so descenders survive, in 300-420ms on cubic-bezier 0.77, 0, 0.18, 1; the new text enters from below 60ms later, words staggered 30ms. Labels beside it slide 12-23px. If the new title wraps to two lines the container animates its height in the same 300ms. The roll follows the direction of navigation (next goes up, previous goes down). It plays only after the visitor's own action, never on load or on scroll. Phone: the same, 260ms. House rules for it: The mask only clips the text itself, no outlined box; whole words roll, never single letters; it runs only after the visitor's own action, so it is not an entrance.
